sn2.12:1.1: Veṇhu (variant _veṇḍu_) is the Pali spelling of Sanskrit _viṣṇu_, who in Pali appears only here and at [dn20:14.1](). He appears somewhat often in the Rig Veda, where he was an ally of Indra in his battle with the constrictor serpent (4.18.11, 6.20.2, 8.100.12). He was the wide-stepping god who made three great strides over the earth, the midspace, and the heavens, opening up the broad expanse of the world
sn2.12:2.1: The common Pali terms _manuja_ (“mankind”, “man”), _manussa_, and _mānava_ all have the same root sense, “child of Manu”. Vishnu himself, under the name Yajña, was a child of Manu via his mother Ākūti, Manu’s daughter.
